healthcareSystem: Universal National Health Insurance (NHI) covers residents. Tourists pay out-of-pocket but costs are very affordable. Excellent quality throughout.
qualityNotes: Excellent healthcare system consistently ranked among the best globally. Modern hospitals with advanced technology. English spoken at major hospitals in Taipei. Very affordable even without insurance.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open daily 9am-10pm. Watson's and Cosmed chains found everywhere. Hospital pharmacies and some chain pharmacies open extended hours.
pharmacyTips: Look for 藥局 (pharmacy) signs. Watson's and Cosmed are major chains. Many medications available OTC at low prices. Pharmacists in Taipei often speak some English.
prescriptionRules: Many medications available OTC that require prescriptions elsewhere. Antibiotics available at pharmacies. Controlled substances require a local prescription.

restrictedMeds.name: Amphetamines/ADHD medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances. Bring documentation and keep in original packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Strong opioids
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly regulated. Bring a doctor's letter and customs declaration.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is strictly illegal in Taiwan. Penalties are severe.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English (and Chinese if possible) for controlled medications. Keep all medicines in original packaging. For large quantities, declare at customs.

travelInsurance.tips: Healthcare in Taiwan is very affordable — an ER visit may cost only $20-50 without insurance. Insurance still recommended for hospital stays and medical evacuation.

recommended: Japanese Encephalitis (for rural areas or extended stays)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations. Ensure routine vaccinations are current.

waterNotes: Tap water should be boiled before drinking in Taiwan. Most hotels and restaurants provide boiled or filtered water. Bottled water is cheap and available everywhere.
foodSafetyTips: Taiwan is a food paradise with excellent food safety at most establishments. Night market food is legendary and generally safe — stick to busy stalls. Fruits should be washed or peeled.
medicalTourismNote: Taiwan is a top medical tourism destination, especially for health checkups, cosmetic surgery, dental care, and Traditional Chinese Medicine. Costs are 50-70% less than the US.
metaDescription: Travel health guide for Taiwan, emergency 119, Cannabis banned, world-class hospitals. Hospital info, pharmacy tips, vaccinations, and travel insurance.

hospitals.name: National Taiwan University Hospital (NTUH)
hospitals.nearTouristArea: Zhongzheng District, Taipei (near Chiang Kai-shek Memorial)
hospitals.notes: Taiwan's top-ranked hospital. International medical service center for foreign patients.

hospitals.name: Taipei Veterans General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Major medical center with international patient services.

hospitals.name: Mackay Memorial Hospital
hospitals.notes: Well-known private hospital. International patient center. Good English service.

pharmacyPhrases.english: I need medicine for a headache

dentalCare.availability: Excellent dental care at very affordable prices. Many dentists speak English in Taipei.
dentalCare.costRange: TWD 500-2,000 ($15-65) for consultation; TWD 1,000-5,000 ($30-160) for fillings
dentalCare.notes: Dental care in Taiwan is excellent and very affordable. Many dental clinics in Taipei cater to international patients.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Major hospitals have dental departments. Many private dental clinics in Taipei offer same-day emergency appointments.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Available in Taipei. Expect TWD 2,000-4,000 ($65-130) per session.
mentalHealth.notes: English-speaking mental health services available in Taipei through international clinics and private practice.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Good accessibility in Taipei. MRT is fully accessible. Improvements continue but older areas may have barriers.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Major hospitals are fully wheelchair accessible with excellent facilities.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Taipei MRT is fully wheelchair accessible. Buses have low floors. Accessible taxis available. YouBike system not wheelchair accessible.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Taipei is generally accessible with good sidewalk infrastructure. Night markets can be crowded. National Palace Museum and major attractions are accessible. Jiufen Old Street has many stairs.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: Masks no longer required. Still commonly worn on public transit.
covidStatus.testing: Tests available at hospitals, clinics, and pharmacies.
covidStatus.notes: Taiwan lifted all COVID restrictions. Some healthcare settings may still request masks.

insuranceClaimProcess: Taiwanese hospitals provide detailed receipts and English-language medical certificates on request. International departments assist with insurance documentation. Costs are low — many travelers pay out-of-pocket. File claims with your insurer within 30 days.
